scope: Small synthetic prototype check; shared scenario families, not a production benchmark.

cases.question: For Q2 2025, report revenue, COGS, operating expenses, operating profit, and gross margin.
human_review: All five values appear correctly in the answer with correct units and period.
Gross margin is not an average of monthly percentages.

cases.question: How much did operating profit change from Q1 to Q2 2025? Reconcile the change across revenue, COGS, and operating expenses.
human_review: Contribution signs are correct and reconcile to the total change.
No unsupported business cause is asserted.

cases.question: Investigate the largest positive account contribution to the Q1-to-Q2 profit change. Compare corresponding months across the quarters and identify the biggest contributing month.
human_review: Select revenue after inspecting the bridge.
April/January, May/February, June/March each add $40,000; report the three-way tie.

cases.question: Was the revenue increase from Q1 to Q2 caused by acquiring more customers?
human_review: Customer acquisition cannot be established from aggregate financial data.
Identify missing customer count, volume, or pricing evidence; no invented cause.

cases.question: For Q2 2025, report revenue, COGS, operating expenses, operating profit, and gross margin.
human_review: All five values appear correctly in the answer with correct units and period.
Gross margin is not an average of monthly percentages.

cases.question: How much did operating profit change from Q1 to Q2 2025? Reconcile the change across revenue, COGS, and operating expenses.
human_review: Contribution signs are correct and reconcile to the total change.
No unsupported business cause is asserted.

cases.question: Investigate the largest negative account contribution to the Q1-to-Q2 profit change. Compare corresponding months across the quarters and identify the biggest contributing month.
human_review: Select COGS after inspecting the bridge.
June versus March has the largest cost increase ($35,000), which contributes negatively to profit.

cases.question: Did higher supplier prices cause the Q1-to-Q2 profit decline?
human_review: Separate the accounting COGS contribution from unproven supplier-price causation.
Ask for unit prices, purchasing volumes, or product mix; no invented business cause.

cases.question: For Q2 2025, report revenue, COGS, operating expenses, operating profit, and gross margin.
human_review: Identify missing May 2025. Full Q2 totals are unavailable.
Do not call observed April+June totals full-quarter results.

cases.question: How much did operating profit change from Q1 to Q2 2025? Reconcile the change across revenue, COGS, and operating expenses.
human_review: No complete-quarter bridge is produced; May is missing.
Request the missing figures instead of filling with zero.

cases.question: Which months are available in each quarter? Is Q2 usable for a complete quarterly comparison?
human_review: Q1 has January, February, March. Q2 has April and June, with May missing.
Reject a complete-quarter comparison.

cases.question: Since reported Q2 profit is $80,000 versus Q1’s $72,000, can I say profit improved by 11.11%?
human_review: Correct the misleading premise: $80,000 covers two months, $72,000 covers three.
Do not endorse 11.11% as the full-quarter profit improvement.
